items.titleEn: The silver trade that cost Felix Zulauf 50%, and why he says gold's fall is different
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – The trade looked easy. It was 1980, gold had just touched $850 an ounce, silver had hit $50 and was sliding, and a 30-year-old Swiss money manager bought it at $36 to catch the bounce. The bounce never came. "I thought I was super smart," Felix Zulauf said. "In a few days, it went from 36 to 18, where I sold. I lost 50%. I lost 50% on my money. I turned the monitor off. Gold, silver remain under pressure as strong GDP, sticky inflation reinforce Fed hike bets - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in early U.S. trading Wednesday, as stronger-than-expected underlying U.S. inflation and resilient economic growth reinforced expectations for another Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December. Gold remained near its lowest level in more than a year, while silver fell below $40.000 an ounce as weakness in industrial commodities compounded the selling. Renewed shipping threats in the Strait of Hormuz provided little support to bullion as monetary policy expectations and concerns about financial-market liquidity continued to dominate trading. Spot gold was trading near $3,482.30 an ounce, down $72.80, or 2.05%, while silver was trading near $39.290 an ounce, down $1.510, or 3.71%, on the session. Gold had traded as low as $3,469.30 during the morning, while silver touched $39.160. Wednesday morning's U.S. economic data reinforced concerns about persistent inflation despite evidence of moderation in some price categories. The October personal consumption expenditures price index increased 0.3% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier, compared with September's annual increase of 3.6%. More significantly, the core PCE index, excluding food and energy, increased 0.3% for a third consecutive month, while annual core inflation accelerated to 3.3% from 3.1%, exceeding expectations for 3.2%. The second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product was revised higher to an annualized 4.3%, indicating continued economic resilience. Personal income increased 0.7% in October, while consumer spending advanced 0.3%. Initial unemployment claims fell to 189,000 , suggesting that labor market conditions remain comparatively firm despite recent evidence of slowing manufacturing activity. Durable goods orders were weaker than expected overall, although core capital goods orders increased 1.2%. The combination of stronger economic growth, resilient employment and persistent underlying inflation reinforced expectations for restrictive Federal Reserve policy, adding to pressure on gold and silver.

Gold prices drop another 1% as US Q3 GDP revised to 4.3% with contained PCE inflation
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Solid economic growth in the third quarter and contained inflation pressures have pushed gold prices back below what some analysts have said is a key support level. The Bureau of Economic Analysis announced that the preliminary reading of third-quarter Gross Domestic Product showed the economy grew 4.3% between July and September, up from the initial estimate of 3.4% and up from 2.2% in the second quarter. The data was better than economists expected, as consensus forecasts were looking for a growth rate of 3.5%. “The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased,” the report said. “Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending.”

items.titleEn: Gold price falls to $3,496/oz after U.S. durable goods rise 0.2% in October
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market is trading near session lows after the latest economic data showed sales of durable goods last month came in below expectations. The Commerce Department announced Wednesday that U.S. durable goods orders rose 0.2% in October, following September’s revised increase of 2.0%. The data was below expectations, as the consensus view of economists called for an increase of 0.4%. Core durable goods, which strip out the volatile transportation sector, rose 0.5% in October, in line with the consensus forecast for a 0.5% reading, while June’s core print was revised at 0.5%.

Gold price approaches $3,500/oz after U.S. weekly jobless claims fall to 189k
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices are trading near $3,500 this morning following the release of better than expected labor market data after the number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits came in below economists’ forecasts. Initial claims for state unemployment benefits came in at a seasonally adjusted 189,000 for the week ending November 21, the Labor Department announced on Wednesday. The number was below expectations, as consensus estimates forecasted a reading of 200,000 claims. The previous week’s figure was revised to 202,000 from 203,000. Meanwhile, the four-week moving average for new claims – often viewed as a more reliable measure of the labor market since it flattens week-to-week volatility – came in at 196,000, against expectations for 196,000 and following the previous week’s revised 197,500 level.
